name: Distributed Tracing Check
description: Conditional (only if observability-tracing.md exists) · Tier B (agentStop): After a session completes, verifies span naming, required instrumentation points, and trace-context propagation.

then.prompt:
## Package Territory Check (MANDATORY — evaluate FIRST)
Before performing any checks below, verify each file's path in your scan.

EXCLUDED ZONES (package infrastructure — NOT compliance subjects):
• .kiro/hooks/ — AI-GCE hook infrastructure
• .kiro/steering/ — AI-DWG/AI-GCE steering infrastructure
• .kiro/agents/ — AI-GCE agent infrastructure
• .governance/ — AI-GCE governance rules/agents/logs
• compliance-log/ — AI-GCE audit trail
• project-initiation/ — AI-PILC output
• architecture/ — AI-ADLC output
• management_framework/ — Shared governance spine
• docs/compliance-* — AI-GCE generated dashboards
• templates/ — AI-DWG planning templates

For each file in your scan: if its path starts with ANY of the above prefixes, SKIP it silently. Only check files outside excluded zones.

---

Check .compliance-state.json → currentPhase. Apply phase-appropriate rules only.

Review instrumentation code touched during this session. Each numbered check names the rule ID it enforces; log that ID in the event below:

1. SPAN NAMING [TRACE-01]: Spans follow the naming convention stated in observability-tracing.md.
2. INSTRUMENTATION POINTS [TRACE-02]: Required instrumentation points (entry handlers, external calls, boundaries) are present.
3. CONTEXT PROPAGATION [TRACE-03]: Trace context is propagated across service and async boundaries.

Only enforce a rule if observability-tracing.md actually generated it (no steering = no rule). If observability-tracing.md is absent from the workspace, this hook is not generated at all.

If tracing gaps are found, warn with the TRACE-* rule ID and the expected convention.
If all rules pass, confirm compliance silently.

## Compliance Logging
After completing all checks, append to `compliance-log/events/{today-date}.jsonl` — ONE event per rule checked, and `ruleId` MUST be the actual rule ID from the check above, NEVER a literal placeholder:
{"timestamp": "{ISO-8601-UTC}", "type": "check", "id": "chk-{date}-{time}-{seq}", "hook": "tracing-check", "trigger": "agentStop", "ruleId": "{the ID from the checked rule, e.g. TRACE-01}", "ruleSeverity": "{severity}", "result": "{pass|fail|warn}", "message": "{finding}"}
Log ONE event per rule checked.
